summary: Eps 58-108 cover manga Part 3 (Souther / Toki-Raoh / Ryuga, ch 83-109, eps 58-77) and Part 4 (Five Chariots + Raoh, ch 110-136, eps 83-109). Two things dominate the structure. First, eps 78-82 are a five-episode retrospective block with no manga counterpart at all (hokuto.fandom's Story Arcs page literally labels the slot 'Recap (episodes 78-82)'), so ep 78 - currently typed canon - is mistyped alongside its already-filler siblings 79-82. Second, Part 4 has an almost exact 27-chapters-over-27-episodes budget but spends four of those episodes on clip shows/anime-original detours (83, 98, 105, 109), so the surviving episodes each carry 1-2 chapters and the anime pads every one of them with original villains. hokuto.fandom carries NO per-episode pages and NO chapter summaries for this range, so the mapping was built from a different reverse index: the character pages' 'appearances = Manga (ch. X-Y), Anime (ep. A-B)' fields, which give hard chapter/episode pin pairs (Belga ch85/ep60, Rizo ch92/ep65, Koko ch101/ep71, Abida+Gonzu ch105/ep73, Huey ch110/ep84-85, Shuren ch111-112/ep86-87, Juza ch113-121/ep88-97, Gelga ch114/ep90, Hiruka ch117-118/ep94-95, Yuria ch120-136/ep96-109, Tou ch115-122/ep83-100, Kim ch125/ep101, Usa ch126/ep102, Fudou ch110-130/ep87-104, Ken-Oh Gundan Doncho ch130-136/ep104-108, Bat+Lin ch1-136/ep1-109), each cross-checked against en.wikipedia's episode summaries and en.wikipedia's chapter-title list. The A1 hit on ep 109 resolves as a junk terminal anchor, not a mistyped row: ep 109 is a clip show by three independent sources, and the honest terminal is ep 108 -> ch 136.

anchors.note: Part 3 opener but almost no manga progress past ep 57's ch 83: hokuto.fandom's Filler page reads '58 - Mostly filler, except for the origin of the Nanto Rokusei Ken', and the Souther/pyramid material here runs ~2 chapters ahead of Souther's ch 85 manga debut. Flat anchor is the truthful reading.

Ch 83 'Nanto in Turmoil!' (Raoh's reflection, the Hyenas, Shu's rebels - Taka and Bull both list Manga ch.83 / Anime ep.59) plus ch 84 'The Furious Dance of Nanto Hakuroken!' when Shu challenges Kenshiro.

Belga is Manga (ch. 85) / Anime (ep. 60), and ch 85's title 'The Star of Hope Awakens!' (Mezameru Jinsei) is exactly ep 60's closing flashback where Shu blinds himself and his Star of Benevolence awakens.
Ch 86 'The Emperor of Nanto!' and ch 87 'The Emperor's Smile!' - Kenshiro's first Souther confrontation. Ryo lists ch.86/ep.62 and Beji and Giji list ch.87/ep.62.
Ch 88 'Shiba Shines Bright!' - Shu's son Shiba/Shiva rescues the captured Kenshiro and dies. Shiva lists Manga (ch. 88) / Anime (ep. 62-63), so the chapter straddles the 62/63 break.
Ch 89 'The Valiant Leader Sheds No Tears!' and ch 90 'The Tragic Star of Hope!' - Shu holds Souther off, is hamstrung and taken. Bracketed by the ch 88/ep 63 and ch 92/ep 65 pins.
Rizo is Manga (ch. 92) / Anime (ep. 65); ch 91 'The Star of Hokuto Quakes!' matches ep 65's beat where Toki and Raoh sense Kenshiro and set out, and ch 91-92's character lists both carry Raoh + Toki.

Shu's death. hokuto.fandom gives Shu Manga (ch. 83-93) / Anime (ep. 55-66) and ch 93 is titled 'A Cruel Miracle!' - Shu regaining his sight seconds before the capstone crushes him, which is precisely ep 66's ending.
Ch 94 'Because of Love!' + ch 95 'Grave Marker of Love!' - Souther's childhood, the sealed chamber and his master Ogai. Rem lists ch.94/ep.67 and Ogai lists ch.94/ep.67-68.

Souther arc END. Souther is Manga (ch. 85-97) / Anime (ep. 58-68); ch 96 'Heaven-Shattering Fist!!' is his Nanto Ho-oken last resort and ch 97 'Fallen Because of Love!' is his death, matching ep 68's summary. Story Arcs page: Souther arc = chapters 83-97 / episodes 58-68.
Brothers arc START. Ch 98 'No Death for Kenoh!' - Raoh recovering in seclusion while Koryu resolves to seal his fists; Koryu is Manga (ch. 98-99) / Anime (ep. 69-70) and Zengyo ch.99/ep.69-70.

Ch 99 'Enduring Soul' is Koryu's death and his sons Zeus and Aus (Manga ch. 99 / Anime ep. 70); ch 100 'That Tragic Day!' is the nuclear-holocaust flashback that ep 69-70 carry. The 99/100 split between eps 69 and 70 is the soft part.
Koko is Manga (ch. 101) / Anime (ep. 71); ch 101 'A Promise from the Past!' is the Ryuken adoption flashback and ch 102 'Awakening Blood!' opens the Raoh-Toki duel, both in ep 71.

Brothers arc END. Story Arcs page: Brothers arc = chapters 98-104 / episodes 69-72. Ch 103 'The Final Farewell!' + ch 104 'A Bond so Strong, So Tragic!' = Raoh tearfully defeating Toki, ep 72's whole content.
Ryuga arc START. Ch 105 'My Star is Tenro!' (Sirius) - Abida and Gonzu both list Manga (ch. 105) / Anime (ep. 73), and Ryuga is Manga (ch. 105-109) / Anime (ep. 73-77).
Ch 106 'The Price of Loyalty!' - Ken-Oh praises Ryuga's loyalty while Ryuga privately judges his tyranny, which is ep 74 end to end. Derived inside the ch 105-109 / ep 73-77 five-for-five arc budget.

Ch 107 'The Testament of Living!' (chapter cast: Raoh, Kokuoh, Ryuga, Kenshiro, Yuria) = ep 75's closing challenge. The bulk of ep 75 - the Sabat village - is anime-original; hokuto.fandom's Filler page marks 75 filler 'except at the end of the episode where Ryuga challenges Kenshiro'.
Ch 108 'Tears of the Tenro!' - Ryuga cuts down Toki to provoke Kenshiro; the chapter's cast (Toki, Kenshiro, Raoh, Kokuoh, Ryuga, Lin, Bat) matches ep 76.

Part 3 END. Ryuga's seppuku-death and Toki's passing = ch 109. Three sources agree the block ends here: Ryuga Manga (ch. 105-109)/Anime (ep. 73-77); Story Arcs 'Ryuga arc (chapters 105-109) / (episodes 73-77)'; Finn Clark 'the ongoing story of episodes 58-77 (anime) or chapters 84-109 (manga)'.

Part 4 story START. Ch 110 'Nanto Finally Rises!!' - Huey mobilising the Wind Brigade against Ken-Oh's outposts. Huey is Manga (ch. 110) / Anime (ep. 84-85). The David / Glenn 'Killer Machine' half is anime-original (David: Anime (ep. 84) only).

Huey's death by a single Ken-Oh punch, the back half of ch 110 - Huey's manga range is the single chapter 110 against anime eps 84-85. His spar with Kenshiro and his brother Shion are anime-original (Shion: Anime (ep. 84-85) only). Flat anchor: one chapter over two episodes.

Ch 111 'The Light that Summons Hokuto!' - Shuren vowing revenge for Huey and burning his own castle. Shuren is Manga (ch. 111-112) / Anime (ep. 86-87). The Morgan half of the episode is anime-original (Morgan: Anime (ep. 86) only).

Ch 112 'The Flames of Devotion!' - Shuren's self-immolating last strike and death (his manga range ends at 112, anime at ep 87). Ep 87 also brings Fudo on screen, whose Anime range starts at ep 87 against a ch 110 manga debut.

Ch 113 'Like a Drifting Cloud!' - Fudo revealed as a Chariot Star and Rihaku's request reaching Juza. Juza is Manga (ch. 113-121) / Anime (ep. 88-97), so his manga and anime debuts pin to this pair exactly.
Still inside ch 113 - Hegu and Daruka both list Manga (ch. 113) / Anime (ep. 89). Flat anchor: ch 113's material is fanned out over eps 88-92 with anime-original padding (Dalko) between.

Ch 114 'Soar, Cloud!' - Gelga storming Juza's castle to reclaim 'his women' and being destroyed. Gelga is Manga (ch. 114) / Anime (ep. 90); Jacob ch.113/ep.90 confirms the 113->114 hand-off lands here.

Ch 115 'Surging Cloud!' - Toh drugs Juza and the Last General unmasks to him. The chapter's cast list (Juza, Tou, Last Nanto General, Rihaku, Yuria) is ep 91's ending exactly, and Tou/Rihaku both list manga debut ch. 115. The Dolfi/Zenda 'democracy' half is anime-original (Zenda: Anime (ep. 91) only).

Ch 116 'The Unconventional Fist!' - Juza and his gang intercepting Ken-Oh's march. Zaku (Manga ch. 113 / Anime ep. 92-94) confirms ep 92 sits at the tail of the ch 113-116 stretch. The hay-cart crossing is anime padding.

Ch 117 'Simply for Love!' - Juza hijacks Kokuoh mid-duel and flees, wounded. The chapter's cast spans Juza/Raoh and the Fudo-village group (Kan, Tanji and Jiro, Hiruka), so ch 117 straddles eps 93-94. The Jenomy assassin is anime-original.

Ch 118 'There is no Death for Me!' - Hiruka throws Tanji and Jiro into the quicksand to force Fudo in. Hiruka is Manga (ch. 117-118) / Anime (ep. 94-95); Kan and Tanji and Jiro list ch. 117-119 / ep. 94-106.

Ch 119 'The Secret Fist of Sorrow!' - Kenshiro turns aside for Fudo's quicksand and destroys Hiruka's Taizan Yoken men. Bounded by the Hiruka ch.118/ep.95 pin above and the Yuria ch.120/ep.96 pin below.

Ch 120 'The Fading Cloud!' - Juza caught in Ken-Oh's fatal hold, and Fudo naming Yuria as the Last General. Yuria's appearances field is Manga (ch. 115, ch. 120-136) / Anime (ep. 89, ep. 96-109): her ch-120 re-entry and her ep-96 re-entry pin to each other.

Ch 121 'To the General!' - Juza's death plus the flashback to the Chariot Stars saving Yuria with Shin's blessing; the chapter's cast (Juza, Yuria, Shin, Rihaku, Tou, Shuren, Huey) is ep 97's content exactly, and Juza's manga range ends at 121 against anime ep 97.

Ch 122 'Distant Desire!' - Toh masquerading as Yuria, her confession to Ken-Oh and her suicide. Tou is Manga (ch. 115-122) / Anime (ep. 83-100) and the chapter cast is Raoh, Kokuoh, Tou, Kenshiro, Ryuken, Yuria.

Ch 123 'The Time Has Come!' - Yuria's escape attempt, Rihaku challenging Ken-Oh, and Kenshiro's first Muso Tensei. The chapter's cast is exactly the four characters of ep 100 (Yuria, Raoh, Rihaku, Kenshiro).
Ch 124 'Torrent of Blood!' (the Muso Tensei spirits) + ch 125 'The Trap of Fate!' - Rihaku's floor trap, Raoh taking Yuria, Kenshiro blinded. Kim is Manga (ch. 125) / Anime (ep. 101).

Ch 126 'Sacrifice to the Demon King!' - Raoh nursed by Yuria, renouncing the Ken-Oh name for 'Demon King' and riding to challenge Fudo. Usa is Manga (ch. 126) / Anime (ep. 102). Running-order END stays 126: the Jado bikers in this episode are pulled forward out of ch 129 (see annotations).

Ch 127 'The Return of the Devil!' (Kijin to narite - Fudo donning his old armour, with the young-Yuria flashback: chapter cast Fudoh, Raoh, Lin, Bat, Ryuken, Yuria) + ch 128 'The Unclouded Fist!' opening the duel.

Ch 129 'Glorious in Defeat!' + ch 130 'Spirit Beyond Body!' - the arrows, Fudo's death, Raoh turning on his own men. Two pins: Fudou is Manga (ch. 110-130) / Anime (ep. 87-104), and the Ken-Oh Gundan Doncho is Manga (ch.130-136) / Anime (eps 104-108).
Ch 131 'Bloodstained Heart!' + ch 132 'Forsaking Love!' (Aete Ai o Tatsu) - Raoh's own men defying him to shield Yuria, and Raoh striking her down. Kokuoh then fetches Kenshiro to Hokuto Renkitoza.
Ch 133 'Crossroads of Fate!' (the two meeting at the training ground) + ch 134 'Strike the Battle Ki!' - Raoh reveals he too has Muso Tensei and the battle auras clash, which is ep 107 end to end.

TERMINAL anchor for the original series, moved here from the filler ep 109. Ch 135 'Blood-Soaked Conqueror!' + ch 136 'Farewell, My Greatest Rival!' Three independent lines fix the series END at ch 136: en.wikipedia's lead ('109 episodes ... adapting the first 136 chapters'), hokuto.fandom's Bat and Lin pages (Manga ch. 1-136 / Anime ep. 1-109), and the Ken-Oh Gundan Doncho pin (ch.136 / ep.108). Ep 108 stops at the fatal blow and the reveal that Yuria was never killed; the last pages of ch 136 land in ep 109's clip show.

continue_points.note: Ep 108 ends mid-ch 136 (fatal blow struck, Raoh not yet dead); the chapter's closing pages - Raoh's farewell, the raised fist, Yuria waking - are held for ep 109's clip-show finale. A reader resuming after ep 108 should read ch 136 itself, not 137.

annotations.note: Five-episode retrospective block with no manga counterpart, inserted between the Ryuga arc (ch 109) and the Five Chariots arc (ch 110): one flashback episode each for Shin, Rei, Yuda, Shu and Souther. hokuto.fandom's Story Arcs table labels the slot 'Recap (episodes 78-82)'; Finn Clark: 'The five subsequent episodes are flashbacks to some of the show's greatest warriors so far'.

Part 4's title episode adapts nothing: it is the anime-original Bugal story (the bath-obsessed tyrant hoarding a thirsty town's water). hokuto.fandom's character pages also give Rihaku and Toh an anime debut of ep 83 against a ch 115 manga debut, i.e. the anime seeds the Nanto capital cast about five chapters early.

Ch 110 alone is stretched across two episodes. Everything outside Huey's mobilisation and his one-punch death is anime-original: David and Glenn the Killer Machine (ep 84), Huey's sparring match with Kenshiro, and Huey's younger brother Shion (both anime-only characters on hokuto.fandom).
Shuren's entire manga presence is two chapters (111-112); the anime gives him two episodes and fills ep 86's other half with the anime-original Morgan, chief of Ken-Oh's vanguard.

Jado and his bikers ambushing the blinded Kenshiro belong to ch 129 ('Glorious in Defeat!', during the Raoh-Fudo duel); the anime lifts them forward into ep 102, before the duel starts. hokuto.fandom gives Jado Manga (ch. 129) / Anime (ep. 102). Running-order END for ep 102 stays 126.

Ch 136 is split across the last two episodes. Ep 108 carries the fight to Raoh's fatal wounding and the Yuria reveal; ep 109 is a clip show of Kenshiro's life whose only new footage is ch 136's closing pages (Raoh's death and farewell, Yuria waking, the two leaving together). Recorded as annotation fact only - ep 109 is a filler row and takes no anchor (A1).

type_corrections.note: Currently canon, but ep 78 is the first of the five recap episodes, not a story episode. Three independent sources: hokuto.fandom Story Arcs table lists 'Recap (episodes 78-82)' as the slot before the Five Chariots arc; hokuto.fandom's Filler page says '78 - Everything except the very beginning is a clip show'; Finn Clark's part-3 review says Part 3 'is really just episodes 58-77. The five subsequent episodes are flashbacks'; en.wikipedia's own summary calls it 'the first in a series of five episodes, each focusing on a different Nanto Seiken warrior'. Eps 79-82 are already typed filler - 78 is the odd row out. AFL types it Manga Canon; AFL is wrong here.

Currently canon. Despite the grand title ('Part Four, the Final Chapter'), the episode is entirely the anime-original Bugal story; ch 110, where the manga's Part 4 starts, contains none of it. hokuto.fandom's Filler page lists 83 flatly under 'Final Chapter'; Finn Clark's part-4 review cites 'the bath-crazed tyrant in the town where everyone's dying of thirst (episode 83)' as one of the show's own inventions; en.wikipedia's summary names no manga character or event. AFL types it Manga Canon.

Currently canon. hokuto.fandom's Filler page lists 61 flatly under 'Ransei Hado Hen'. Corroborating: every named character in en.wikipedia's ep 61 summary (Jay, Ami, Galzas/Garzus, Suwanny village) is absent from the hokuto.fandom character lists of ch 85-86, the chapters flanking this slot, and none has a wiki page with a manga appearance. AFL types it Manga Canon.

hokuto.fandom's Filler page lists both under 'Final Chapter' as filler, but that page overshoots: the same wiki's character pages put Huey (Manga ch. 110 / Anime ep. 84-85) in ep 84 and Shuren (Manga ch. 111-112 / Anime ep. 86-87) in ep 86, and en.wikipedia's summaries carry that manga material. Each episode pairs it with a wholly anime-original half (David and Glenn in 84, Morgan in 86 - both anime-only per hokuto.fandom). Mixed is the honest type; they keep their anchors under A1.

hokuto.fandom's Filler page marks each of these as filler with an explicit carve-out - '58 - Mostly filler, except for the origin of the Nanto Rokusei Ken', '75 - Except at the end of the episode where Ryuga challenges Kenshiro', '91 - Up until the ending where the General reveals herself to Juza' - and en.wikipedia's summaries match that shape in all three (Souther's on-screen debut in 58 runs ahead of his ch 85 manga debut; the Sabat village in 75 and the Dolfi/Zenda 'democracy' town in 91 are anime-original, Zenda being an anime-only character). All three currently read canon via AFL. Mixed, and all three keep their anchors under A1.

repairs.why: A1 triage, fork resolved as JUNK ANCHOR rather than mistyped row. Ep 109 is a clip show and the row type is right: hokuto.fandom's Filler page lists '109 - Clip show' with no carve-out (that page does add carve-outs elsewhere - '57 - Clip show until Rei's death at the end', '78 - Everything except the very beginning', '91 - Up until the ending' - so the flat listing is deliberate); AFL types it Filler; en.wikipedia's summary is 'A summary is presented of Kenshiro's life, from the day he first met Yuria as a child to his final battle against Raoh'. The stored 136 is terminal inflation - the last chapter of the series parked on the last episode of the series. Nulling it costs no position: ep 108 already reaches ch 136 (Ken-Oh Gundan Doncho ch.136/ep.108; Bat and Lin ch. 1-136 / ep. 1-109), so the new ep-108 anchor carries the same terminal with a continue point of 136, and the residue that genuinely plays in ep 109 - ch 136's closing pages - is recorded as an annotation instead. Manual-tier row, so no re-derive risk.

structure.notes: Two components, cumulative numbering already correct: Hokuto no Ken eps 1-109 = manga ch 1-136; Hokuto no Ken 2 eps 110-152 = ch 137-210 (ch 211-245 never animated). Confirmed three ways: en.wikipedia's lead ('lasted 109 episodes ... adapting the first 136 chapters ... a sequel series ... adapts chapters 137 to 210'), hokuto.fandom's Bat and Lin pages (Manga ch. 1-136, 136.5-160 / Anime ep. 1-109, 110-122), and the ch 137 pins Joe and Mamu (Manga ch. 137 / Anime ep. 110). In-season part boundaries within eps 58-108: Part 3 = eps 58-77 = ch 83/84-109 (Souther arc ch 83-97 / eps 58-68; Brothers arc ch 98-104 / eps 69-72; Ryuga arc ch 105-109 / eps 73-77); recap block eps 78-82; Part 4 = eps 83-109 = ch 110-136 (Five Chariots ch 110-130 / eps 83-105; Raoh ch 131-136 / eps 106-109). CHAPTER SPACE: the 245-chapter / 27-volume tankobon numbering used by both en.wikipedia's chapter list and hokuto.fandom, which is what this file uses; volume boundaries in the context file were re-verified against en.wikipedia volumes 10-16 and match exactly (v10 81-89, v11 90-98, v12 99-107, v13 108-116, v14 117-125, v15 126-134, v16 135-143). BONUS CHAPTER: hokuto.fandom carries 'HnK Chapter 136.5 - He Who Rides With Me' (the 2014 Comic Zenon special, ja.wikipedia: 245 chapters plus 1 special) sitting between 136 and 137 - it is not adapted and must never be folded into mainline numbering. Ch 83 appears to be split across eps 57-59 (its opening in ep 57, whose stored anchor is 83, and its Taka/Bull material in ep 59 per those characters' pages) with ep 58 as padding in between; the stored ep-57 record is defensible as END-in-running-order and was left untouched per task scope.

flags_for_sean: TYPE-SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (the reason 6 of the 8 type_corrections above exist): the stored types come from animefillerlist, which types eps 58, 61, 75, 78, 83, 84, 86 and 91 all 'Manga Canon' - even though it does use its 'Mixed Canon/Filler' label 14 times elsewhere in this series. hokuto.fandom's own Filler page contradicts AFL on every one of those eight. I sided with hokuto.fandom (corroborated per episode by en.wikipedia summaries, anime-only character pages and Finn Clark) but this is a systematic AFL-vs-wiki split, not eight independent judgements - worth ruling once rather than row by row.

A1 FORK, alternative branch for the record: ep 109's residue is NOT a <=5-page sliver - it is the closing pages of ch 136 (Raoh's death and farewell, Yuria waking, Kenshiro and Yuria leaving), i.e. the actual ending of the original series wrapped inside a clip show. If you would rather keep the position on 109, the consistent form is a type_correction 109 -> mixed and keeping end_chapter 136, which would also match the precedent of the stored ep 57 (a clip show with Rei's death at the end, typed canon and anchored to 83). I recommend the repair as written - three sources call 109 a clip show and ep 108 already carries the same terminal - but the call is yours.

STORED AIR DATES ARE WRONG on several rows in this range, inherited from animefillerlist (which has known date errors here). Per en.wikipedia: ep 81 = 1986-07-24 (stored 1986-10-24), ep 82 = 1986-07-31 (stored 1986-10-31), ep 85 = 1986-08-21 (stored 1986-08-12), ep 90 = 1986-10-16 (stored 1986-10-19), ep 96 = 1986-11-27 (stored 1987-11-27), ep 108 = 1987-02-26 (stored 1987-03-26 - which is actually ep 112's date). Out of scope for anchors; raising it because the stored order/date pairs currently look scrambled around eps 79-85.

OPEN FLAG #688 (count_mismatch, MU latest chapter 71 vs AniList 245): the reading edition is the 245-chapter / 27-volume Shueisha tankobon, which is what en.wikipedia's chapter list, hokuto.fandom and AniList all use, and ja.wikipedia states the run as 245 chapters plus one special. MU's 71 matches no known edition's chapter count and should not be treated as this series' chapter space.

hokuto.fandom has NO per-episode pages (only 6 'HnK Episode N' pages exist wiki-wide, none in 58-109) and NO chapter summaries for ch 83-137 (all '{{Expand section}}'). Anyone re-verifying this series should go straight to the character pages' 'appearances' fields and the chapter pages' cast lists - that is where the chapter/episode pairs live.
